title: Ketchaponack
summary: Ketchaponack is a Southampton placename for a neck of land in the Westhampton Beach area, in the western part of Southampton town on Quantuck Creek near the historic West Hampton post office area.
address_label: General Ketchaponack / Quantuck Creek area, Westhampton Beach, New York
translation_content:
Recorded spellings include Ketcheponack, Catchponack, Catchaponack, Ketchabonack, Ketchabonnack, and Catcheboneck. Potunk appears in related Westhampton source context but is also maintained as its own nearby placename record. The name has been connected with large edible roots or yellow water lily, though that interpretation should be checked against the original source.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names also embody a sense of belonging to a place, coexistence with the natural world and the longstanding relationship between a People and their place; they anchor the past to the present.”

— Bob Joseph, The Relationship Between Indigenous Peoples and Place Names (2016), Article paragraph 12
land_loss_content: Ketchaponack ties a Native placename to a named neck, creek, marsh, and later town-record landscape. Indigenous place names remained in local boundary descriptions, land records, and neighborhood memory.
whereintheworld_content: Ketchaponack is associated broadly with Quantuck Creek and the Westhampton Beach area. The sources do not establish an exact historic boundary.
